item.title: Chicago Fire - Do Not Resuscitate - Review : Actors, Policemen and Family
item.description: I really liked this episode of Chicago Fire, we got some further introduction to some new characters and got some good moments from our OG characters. I absolutely loved the whole Herrmann storyline of this episode, anytime we get to see Hermmann be in his grumpy mood is great. He is no stranger to different ventures so it genuinely wouldn’t be too far fetched for Herrmann to venture into acting and this was a very good start. I will forever adore that we get to see Herrmann using his flip phone

item.title: Chicago PD - Live And Die By Your CI - Review : Who Is The Good Guy?
item.description: This was a fantastic Chicago PD episode. This season has been great episode after great episode and this was no different. It is great to have Ruzek back, and it was such a perfect episode focussing on him. I loved that we got to see Ruzek have a path of growth throughout this episode. Every conversation that he had landed him in the place where he could finally be okay with moving house and putting Mack and Burgess first and it was lovely to see. item.title: When On-Screen Chemistry Creates Unreal Standards for Cross-Cultural Relationships
item.description: There is a reason people get wrecked by fictional couples. A glance across a hallway. A fight that turns flirtatious. One long pause in the rain. Then boom — viewers are sold. It feels electric, rare, almost unfair. Television knows how to push that button. It can make two people seem destined in less than three minutes.
